fruits_veggies.title: Fruits & Veggies: What to Do With Them
fruits_veggies.text: A practical kitchen guide to everyday fruits and vegetables: how to pick them, store them, and bring out their best flavors.

items.title: Avocados
items.text: Check firmness near the stem. Mash with lime juice, minced garlic, and flaky sea salt for guacamole, slice over crusty sourdough toast, or blend into creamy smoothies.

items.title: Heirloom & Cherry Tomatoes
items.text: Store at room temperature to protect natural sweetness. Slow-roast cherry tomatoes with olive oil and garlic for pasta, or slice heirlooms with mozzarella and fresh basil.

items.title: Spinach & Leafy Greens
items.text: Keep dry in the crisper drawer lined with a paper towel. Flash-sauté with garlic and chili flakes, fold into morning eggs, or toss raw into fresh grain bowls.

items.title: Citrus (Lemons & Oranges)
items.text: Zest the peel before juicing to extract rich aromatic oils. Use the bright acidity to lift pan sauces and vinaigrettes, or slice into ice water for daily refreshment.

items.title: Carrots & Sweet Potatoes
items.text: Store in a cool, dark pantry away from moisture. Toss with olive oil, smoked paprika, and rosemary, then roast hot (400°F / 200°C) until caramelized and crispy-edged.

items.title: Fresh Berries
items.text: Rinse in cool water only right before serving to avoid mold. Spoon over morning oats and greek yogurt, bake into rustic muffins, or simmer into a quick 5-minute compote.
